reasoning: Reproduced. Bench facts are drawn uniformly per relation (facts.py:46-55), so answers follow KB object frequencies while chance is 1/len(options) (suite.py:170) and 0 for exact items. I recomputed on the frozen knowledge draw: a subject-blind per-relation majority-object picker gets 0.37 on the 150 MC items (animal_legs 11/16, animal_class 9/16, baby_animal 7/15, vehicle_travel 7/15) and 0.26 on the 50 exact items, which normalizes to 19.1. Over 40 other draws it averages 0.40 MC and 0.22 exact, so the skew is systematic. The Task 16 ruling (line 201) only tested one global constant reply, and ADR 0001 rule 1's claim that a constant guesser earns exactly 1/N assumes uniform answers; neither covers per-relation priors. Impact is a miscalibrated floor of about 15-19 for models that have learned relation priors but no subject facts. It does not change G3's pass/fail, which compares mixes. Fix before bench-v1 freezes.
fix_recommendation: Make the answer distribution uniform within each relation before bench-v1 freezes. In facts.py, replace the uniform fact draw used for knowledge_bench_items and consistency_groups with a stratified one: per relation, cycle through the relation's distinct objects (round-robin in a seeded order, skipping objects whose bench-eligible facts are exhausted) and take a random unused fact for each. Distractors from kb.distractors are already uniform over the other objects, so the option set is then exchangeable and a subject-blind picker gets 1/4. Add a regression test that a KB-frequency-prior picker (per-relation most common object, the code in the verdict probe) scores 0.25 +/- 0.07 on knowledge MC and no more than about 0.10 on exact items. Regenerate any pinned frozen-draw expectations. Alternative: measure the floor as the instruction category does.
